statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is in the low band because CME equity futures are closed and the last observed tape was orderly, while Stress stays high on the pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop and a fresh weekend Hormuz escalation.
recommendation: Tail remains below the caution threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. One narrow window is flagged: the 22:00-00:00 UTC Globex weekend reopen, where unpriced weekend headlines meet thin liquidity and the mapped state there is WATCH.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closed and orderly into a hawkish Fed week, with a fresh Hormuz strike and Monday's Muscat talks framing the Sunday reopen
body: CME equity futures are shut until 22:00 UTC, so no live NQ price path exists at assessment time. The last observed tape is Friday's: the Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51-29,473.12 range and about 105 points below the session high, so the index was not pinned at an extreme, while VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84. That structure is orderly and retracement-friendly, which keeps Tail in the low band. The backdrop is markedly more tense. Treasury yields sit at 4.95% on the 10-year, 4.56% on the 2-year and 5.37% on the 30-year; WTI is near $100.05 and Brent near $104.61 after a roughly 9.7% weekly gain; and markets price roughly an 86% chance of a 25 basis point hike at Wednesday's FOMC under Chair Kevin Warsh. Equities near highs with VIX under 16 against that stack is a thin cushion, which is why Stress is high while Tail is not. Two weekend developments cut in opposite directions: UKMTO reported a vessel struck in the Strait of Hormuz late Saturday, with a fire and crew evacuation, while Iran and Gulf states are due to meet in Muscat on Monday on an Omani framework for reopening the strait. Conflicting headlines of that kind raise dispersion rather than establish the persistent no-retracement path Tail measures. The 22:00 UTC reopen is the single concentrated risk point inside the next 24 hours; Wednesday's multi-stage Fed sequence falls outside this window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available and uniformly green with the mapped state EA_ON. Tail was flat at 6 through late Saturday and the overnight hours, then drifted up from 05:00 UTC to peak at 17 by 15:00 UTC as the weekend ran toward the futures reopen, easing to 16 in the final hour. Stress rose steadily from 50 to 71 as the pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop accumulated, the dominant mode stayed normal throughout, and Confidence held near 86 before stepping down to 71 in the last hour as the weekend evidence gap widened.
outlookSummary: The window splits into three phases. Until 22:00 UTC the CME equity complex is closed and no price path can form, so Tail holds in the low band and rises only as a forward allowance into the reopen. The 22:00-00:00 UTC Globex reopen is the single concentrated risk point, where two days of Hormuz, Ukraine and Fed-expectation news reprice into thin liquidity; Tail enters the watch band for those two hours as a conditional gap allowance rather than an observed move. From the Asian hours onward the base case is absorption of the gap and a return to two-way trade, with Tail decaying toward 17 and modest upticks at the European open and the 13:30 UTC US cash open. Monday's US calendar holds only low-importance bill auctions, so residual risk is headline-driven, with crude the main transmission channel and Monday's Muscat meeting an unresolved checkpoint. Stress stays in the high band throughout because the underlying tension - a live hike debate, the 10-year near 5% and crude near $100 - is unresolved. Confidence starts in the solid band and improves into the high band once a live tradable price path exists again.
